sample_unit: CT images (two public datasets: BHX and RSNA 2019+)
models_evaluated: six deep learning detectors (CNN one-stage, two-stage, RT-DETR variant)

links.outcome: Performance drop under cross-dataset external validation due to domain shift and dataset differences
links.effect: External validation showed substantial degradation; Swin-RT-DETR BB-DSC reductions of ~0.54-0.79 (BHX-to-RSNA+) and 0.17-0.74 (RSNA+-to-BHX).
links.quote: External validation showed substantial performance degradation across architectures, subtypes, and validation directions.

links.outcome: Overestimated performance from internal validation versus external test data
links.effect: Internal validation showed competitive performance, but external testing revealed substantial degradation with attenuation of architecture-specific advantages under domain shift.
links.quote: Although Transformer-based hierarchical feature extraction showed subtype-dependent advantages under internal validation, these advantages diminished under bidirectional external validation.

unlisted_practices: Dataset characterization (subtype prevalence, bounding-box geometry, annotation density) before model evaluation
Patient-level evaluation in addition to image-level evaluation

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the cross-dataset generalizability and domain shift degradation of multiple deep learning architectures for intracranial hemorrhage detection on public CT datasets, without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
